title: sticky-circuit-parking-and-penalty-dampener
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: we observed repeated circuit reopen/flap cycles during tenant spikes leading to large SLO penalty thrashing and KV cache invalidations. This change introduces a "sticky park" state for circuits and a penalty-dampener in the SLO enforcer to reduce oscillation under bursty traffic. What this PR does: 1) Adds a 'parked' circuit state that persists for a configurable minimum window and exposes reasons (capacity, latency, backend-fail) for auditing; this prevents immediate reopen attempts after transient failures. 2) Reworks the SLO enforcer penalty application to use a decoupled dampening function (exponential decay with hysteresis and a capped carry-over) to avoid multi-tenant penalty amplification. 3) Adds an opt-in annotation and config flag to enable sticky-parking per-tenant and a global SLO_DAMPENER_FACTOR so we can ramp safely. 4) Adjusts KV drain ordering to prefer warm-to-cold transitions when a circuit parks to reduce cache churn. 5) Adds telemetry and dashboards: slo_enforcer.penalty_dampener, circuit.park_duration_seconds, circuit.park_reason, and slo_enforcer.penalty_recovery_rate. 6) Includes unit and integration tests that simulate spike/reopen patterns, and a new canary job to validate behavior in a regional failover. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, default OFF for existing customers; we will enable for a small subset of internal tenants for 24h, collect metrics, then progressively expand. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linked: ENG-2147) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests (regional canary) - [x] Metrics + dashboards - [x] Docs and runbook updates - [x] Backport/hotfix for recent incident (SUP-9821) Runtime safety: sticky park uses a bounded TTL and respects manual overrides; SLO dampener preserves safety by bounding the maximum penalty and exposing a debug switch. See runbook section at docs/deploy/failover-runbook.md; also this PR includes a short note on rollback steps. Notes: this is intentionally conservative; we prioritized observability and a narrow config surface to reduce blast radius.
